title: Showcase: live debate
summary: Debate a parent live on whether kids should be paid for chores, then run this week's Sprout card with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part.

steps.title: Live against a parent
steps.body:
This debate is live, against a real person, not against Rebut. Pick a parent to debate and agree on the motion: 'Kids should be paid for chores.' Three rounds, and alternate who speaks first each round.

Round 1: before you make your own point, steelman the side you are arguing against. Say the other person's best point first, in your own words, the real one, not a weak version. Then give your own claim, reason and example.

Round 2: ask one cross-examination question. Listen for a word like 'always', 'never' or 'everyone' in what the other person just said, or a reason that only covers part of the claim, and ask a question that shows the gap. Let them answer before you respond.

Round 3: make your strongest closing point. Keep every turn to one point, said once. If you catch yourself stacking a second point onto the first, stop and save it for the next round: a debate that never lands one point clearly is harder to follow than one that lands three.

steps.title: Teach someone younger
steps.body:
A parent card is the short card in the app that a grown-up normally uses with Sprout. It has a title, a list of three to five steps to do together, and two or three "things to notice" while you do them.

This week you are the one running it, not a grown-up, same as showcase week 4. Open this week's Sprout parent card from Sprout's screen, and read it once, all the way through, before you start, so you know what is supposed to happen.

Then run the card with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part. Let them do the actual activity, the sorting, the counting, the pattern, whatever the card asks for. Your job is to read the prompts and notice what they do, not to do it for them.

Watch for one thing they do that surprises you, something they get right that you did not expect, or a way they solve it that is not how you would have.
checklist: I let them do it, I did not do it for them
I noticed one thing they could do that surprised me

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the live debate, all three rounds, phone propped up so both of you are in frame.
